messages.content:
We are stopping our own work on this competition, so here are the numbers we collected in case they save someone GPU hours. Everything below is the public Milestone 2 notebook by Daniel Franzen (thanks for publishing it), run on Kaggle's RTX Pro 6000, 25 public games x 2 passes per run, with per-game scores read from the notebook's own per-game output.

1. Run-to-run noise is large

We ran the same code twice (no changes between the two runs):

  • Run A: mean 47.30
  • Run B: mean 48.92
  • Per-game score difference between the two runs: standard deviation 24.0 points
  • 7 of 25 games differed by more than 20 points (largest: -78.8 and +50.0)

With 25 games x 2 passes, that puts the standard error of a run mean at roughly +/-4.8. In practice we could only trust offline differences of about 10 points or more. Anything smaller needs repeated runs of both arms. This matches what Son Pham reported for online copies of the same notebook (mean 25.77, std 3.93).

Online, 2 of our 12 submissions came back as "Succeeded" with a public score of 0.00. One of them was the unmodified notebook. We never found the cause.

2. Negative result: 14 concurrent games instead of 10

We changed ARC3_MAX_ACTIVE_STREAMS, MAXREQ and CUDAGRAPH_MAXBS from 10 to 14 and changed nothing else.

  • Mean 29.90 vs 47.30 for the baseline. 14 streams won 7 games, the baseline won 17. Median 13.81 vs 41.67.
  • The baseline held about 600-620 generated tok/s for the whole run. With 14 streams, cumulative throughput peaked around 470 tok/s and fell to about 344, so late in the run it was near 280 tok/s.
  • Total generated tokens: 5.07M vs 8.74M.

Our reading: with the 136k context and FP8 KV cache, 10 streams is already close to what the KV cache can hold. More streams makes every stream slower once contexts grow. The 14-stream machine also had slower disk (model preload 837 s vs 219 s), but that only explains a late start, not the halved throughput in the second half.

3. Negative result: ending a game when one level stalls

In the baseline, 19.3% of generated tokens were spent after a game's last level-up. The median gap between level-ups was 19.8k tokens. The largest gap that still ended in a level-up was 104k tokens.

So we tried ending a game once the current level had used 110k tokens, and giving the freed slot to games that were still progressing.

  • Mean 38.97, vs 48.11 for the average of the two baseline runs: -9.1. Paired by game: 10 wins, 11 losses, 4 ties.
  • Games it cut (for example r11l at level 1/6 and ar25 at level 6/8) were fully cleared in both baseline runs.
  • The deep games we hoped to help cleared fewer levels, not more.

So a level that has eaten 110k tokens is still often solvable. We did not try higher thresholds, since there is little room left above 110k.

Takeaways

  • Treat a single offline run (or a single submission) of this harness as a draw from a wide distribution. Compare arms with repeated runs, or only act on large differences.
  • On this hardware, the concurrency and early-stopping knobs we tried were already at or near their best in the public notebook.

messages.content:
We resubmitted the exact same notebook version and the score fell from 32.76 to 24.03. All three of our runs on Oct 18–20 (different versions) landed at 24–27, while all three on Oct 15–17 landed at 31–33. The same thing happened Oct 11–14. Every run completes the full 9 hours, and our harness sends a keep-alive move so the 15-minute idle rule can't stop the scoring. Has anyone else seen identical submissions drop recently?

Hosts: was anything changed in the scoring gateway or the submission hardware around Oct 11 or Oct 18?

messages.content:
Title: Do submission reruns count against the weekly GPU quota? (quota dropped with nothing running)

Hi all, and hosts,

A question about GPU quota accounting for this competition, in case others have seen the same.

  • My two scored submissions each ran the full ~9h budget on the RTX PRO 6000.
  • On Oct 19 my quota went from 4h 25m (01:14 UTC) to 0h 1m (03:49 UTC), although no notebook or session of mine was running during that time. My second submission had already finished ("Succeeded") about 9 hours after I submitted it.

Questions:

  1. Are competition reruns charged to the weekly 30h GPU quota, and at what rate for the RTX PRO 6000?
  2. Can a rerun's usage be applied after it finishes (a delayed charge), which would explain the drop?
  3. How are others planning around ~3 full-length submissions per week before the Nov 2 deadline?

I've also emailed Kaggle support. Any experience or official clarification would be much appreciated. Thanks!

If you don't do any move for 15 minutes, the run will end with the score so far - 0.00 in your case since you didn't do anything yet.

You can start a thread that issues a RESET move to one game every 10 minutes until startup to deal with this.

messages.content:
My last two submissions (Oct 16 and Oct 17 UTC) both scored 0.00 and were marked complete within about 4.5 hours of submitting, so they ended well before the 9 h limit. Both are Franzen's M2 SGLang notebook with small harness changes. A nearly identical version scored 26.92 on Oct 15, with the same harness patch and image pin and only two scheduler settings changed. Earlier variants scored 27 to 30, and the Save & Run commits still finish normally.

Is anyone else getting 0.00 or early exits since the site update around Oct 14–15? Hosts, could you check whether something changed in the scoring environment, like the gateway, the machines, or a runtime limit?

Slow∞Loop reported the same symptom here: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/arc-prize-2026-arc-agi-3/discussion/750127
